title: Modules and Imports
description: Organize your code into modules. Learn to import, export, and structure larger BPL projects.
objectives: Import functions and types from modules
Export your own functions and types

sections.title: Why Modules?
sections.content:
As programs grow, you need to:

- **Organize** code into logical units
- **Reuse** code across projects
- **Hide** implementation details
- **Avoid** name conflicts

BPL's module system lets you split code into files, import what you need, and export what others can use.

sections.title: Import Syntax Comparison

languages.Python:
from std import io
import myfile
languages.JavaScript:
import { IO } from 'std/io';
import myFunc from './myfile';

sections.explanation: BPL uses import/from syntax similar to JavaScript/TypeScript, with explicit file extensions.

sections.title: Exporting Your Code

lineExplanations.3: export keyword makes functions available to importers.
lineExplanations.20: Without export, functions are private to the file.

sections.title: Standard Library Overview
sections.content:
BPL includes a growing standard library:

| Module | Purpose | Key Functions |
|--------|---------|---------------|
| `std/io.bpl` | Input/Output | printString, printInt, readLine |
| `std/string.bpl` | String operations | length, concat, substring |
| `std/math.bpl` | Math functions | abs, min, max, pow |
| `std/collections.bpl` | Data structures | Vec, Map, Set |
| `std/fs.bpl` | File system | readFile, writeFile |
| `std/time.bpl` | Time operations | now, sleep |

Import what you need:
```bpl
import [IO] from "std/io.bpl";
import [Math] from "std/math.bpl";
```

sections.title: Project Structure
sections.content:
For larger projects, organize files by functionality:

```
my_project/
├── main.bpl           # Entry point
├── bpl-package.json   # Package config
├── src/
│   ├── utils.bpl      # Utility functions
│   ├── models/
│   │   ├── user.bpl   # User struct
│   │   └── order.bpl  # Order struct
│   └── services/
│       ├── auth.bpl   # Authentication
│       └── data.bpl   # Data access
└── tests/
    └── utils.test.bpl # Tests
```

**Import paths:**
- `"std/..."` - Standard library
- `"./file.bpl"` - Same directory
- `"../file.bpl"` - Parent directory
- `"./dir/file.bpl"` - Subdirectory

sections.title: Module Best Practices
sections.expectedOutput:
Config valid: 1
Process 50: 100
Invalid input!
Process 150: -1

lineExplanations.10: Private helper - not exported, internal use only.

sections.title: Module Guidelines
sections.content:
**DO:**
✅ Export only the public API
✅ Use clear, descriptive names
✅ Group related functionality
✅ Document exported items
✅ Keep modules focused (single responsibility)

**DON'T:**
❌ Export internal helpers
❌ Create circular dependencies
❌ Put everything in one huge file
❌ Use vague module names like "utils" or "misc"

sections.title: Practice: Create a Math Module
sections.instructions:
Create functions that would belong in a math module:
- `abs(n: int) ret int` - absolute value
- `max(a: int, b: int) ret int` - larger of two
- `min(a: int, b: int) ret int` - smaller of two
- `clamp(val: int, lo: int, hi: int) ret int` - constrain to range

Test them all in main.
sections.hint: abs: if n < 0 return -n. clamp: if val < lo return lo, if val > hi return hi.

sections.title: Key Takeaways
sections.content:
✅ **import [Name] from "path"** brings in modules

✅ **export** makes items available to importers

✅ Standard library: `"std/module.bpl"`

✅ Local files: `"./file.bpl"` or `"../file.bpl"`

✅ **extern** imports C functions

✅ Keep modules **focused** and **well-organized**

✅ Export only the **public API**

questions.question: What does 'import [IO] from "std/io.bpl"' do?
questions.explanation: This imports the IO module from BPL's standard library.

questions.question: How do you make a function available to other files?
questions.explanation: Use the 'export' keyword before the frame declaration.

questions.question: What does extern do?
questions.explanation: extern declares a function that's defined externally, typically in C.
